claims.head: The Maple Leafs give up shots, and the Avalanche take them
claims.call: The Avalanche take at least their usual 70.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot like the Avalanche, and the Maple Leafs are one of the league’s worst at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Maple Leafs’ end.
claims.nums: Colorado 1st for shot volume (70.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Toronto 28th for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Avalanche shoot a lot, and the Maple Leafs give up plenty.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 5 games this season

check.measure: 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, adjusted for score and venue
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Turnovers could swing this one
claims.call: The Avalanche get at least their usual 7.7% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Avalanche turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Maple Leafs are near the bottom of the league at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Maple Leafs.
claims.nums: Colorado 6th for chances off turnovers (7.7% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Toronto 24th for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Avalanche pounce on loose pucks, and the Maple Leafs cough them up.

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals within 5 seconds of winning the puck
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Expect a track meet
claims.call: The game runs at more than 89.0 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.body: Toronto plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Colorado. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
claims.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Toronto 5th (84.4), Colorado 1st (89.0)
claims.gist: Both teams like a fast game.

check.rule: held if tonight's pace is above the faster team's usual; partly if above the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Avalanche kill penalties far better than the Maple Leafs
claims.body: The Avalanche are one of the league’s best for the penalty kill, at the airtight end; the Maple Leafs are the league’s worst, at the leaky end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Avalanche and the Maple Leafs sit at opposite ends for penalty kill.
claims.call: The Avalanche’s penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Maple Leafs’.

check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: J. Tavares is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
O. Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 6% last season.

COL.head: A big edge for Colorado
COL.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games, Toronto will be without Tavares, and Colorado has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Toronto can make a game of it if they pounce on loose pucks.

TOR.head: A steep climb for Toronto
TOR.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games, Toronto will be without Tavares, and Colorado has home ice. Toronto could still pull it off if they pounce on loose pucks, but they might need a miracle.

story.head: Roy meets his old team
paras: The Maple Leafs come in at 2-2-1, the Avalanche at 3-1-0.
The Avalanche shoot a lot, and the Maple Leafs give up plenty. Both teams like a fast game.
